title: Sprint buffer funding & hire-velocity chooser (scenario lab)
content:
Purpose:
Quick experiment matrix to choose between (A) dedicated sprint buffer fund vs (B) contingent hire pool for handling short-term token demand surges and feature-driven bursts. Connects pricing sensitivity outputs to near-term hiring velocity decisions.

Status/context:
- Working sheet for FY27 planning window; intended to give PMs and Eng leads a simple decision surface they can use during weekly planning.
- Background: recent spike in beta customer usage (early Nov) consumed burst reserve and pushed latency-sensitive routes into higher-cost GPU mix. We need a repeatable rule: when to spend buffer dollars vs. onboard short-term contractors vs. accelerate perm hires.
- This is intentionally lightweight — assumes finance + talent ops + infra will run triggers.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Current headcount (company): 148 FTEs
- Average fully-burdened cost per perm-engineer (SE/ML infra): $220k/year (~$18.3k/month)
- Average contractor rate (equiv. SE): $10k/month (variable, includes agency fees)
- Marginal per-token inference cost on current stack: $0.0008/token (steady-state); during degraded routing to on-demand GPUs cost jumps to $0.0025/token
- Typical surge event duration: 2–6 weeks
- Buffer fund target: $250k (one-time pool to finance burst capacity leasing and spot GPU top-ups)

Scenario chooser table (simplified):
Columns: Scenario | Trigger metric | Immediate action | 6-week cost estimate | Net unit-econ delta | Hiring recommendation
Rows:
1) Small surge | +15% sustained token volume vs. baseline over 7d | Draw from sprint buffer (up to $25k) + throttle low-priority routes | $18k (burst GPU + network) | -0.03% gross margin impact | No hires; monitor
2) Medium surge | +40% sustained token volume over 7d OR runway risk > 12w | Use buffer up to $100k + onboard 2 contractors (6w) | $96k (burst + 2 contractors) | -0.7% gross margin impact | Hire 2 contractors, backfill via perm hire evaluation after 12w
3) Prolonged shift | >30% increase for 6w and still rising | Approve contingent hire pool (3–6 contractors) + priority quantization rollout | $220k (contractors + burst + quant infra) | -1.6% gross margin (temporary) | Convert 1–2 best contractors to perm if sustained >12w
4) Price sensitivity stress | Model: per-token price increases by 60% due to routing to on-demand | Immediate: enable price-tiering for non-critical customers + enable reserve throttles | $payload depends on lost revenue vs. saved infra; estimate net -2.5% margin if unmanaged | Consider pausing low-commit features and escalate sales credits approval

Quick numeric worked example (Medium surge):
- Baseline monthly tokens: 75B tokens
- Surge delta: +40% => additional 30B tokens for the surge month
- Marginal cost steady-state: 30B * $0.0008 = $24,000 (if served on normal infra)
- If routed to on-demand: 30B * $0.0025 = $75,000
- Incremental infra premium = $51,000
- Contractors (2 * $10k/month * 1.5 months avg) = $30,000
- Buffer spend estimate = $81,000 -> round to $96k in scenario table to allow slack (30% overhead for ops + data egress)

Headcount velocity vs. buffer tradeoff (decision heuristics):
- If expected surge recurring probability < 25% over next 6 months => prefer buffer usage over perm hires.
- If expected surge recurrence probability > 40% and duration expectation > 8 weeks => prioritize perm hire (start 12-week recruitment pipeline immediately).
- Use contractors as bridging mechanism when expected duration is 4–12 weeks.

Buffer pool sizing sensitivity (toy grid):
- Buffer $100k => covers ~2 medium surges/year (best-effort, higher throttling risk)
- Buffer $250k => covers ~5 medium surges or 1 prolonged shift without immediate hires
- Buffer $500k => covers multiple prolonged shifts; increases cash runway pressure but reduces emergency credit draws

Policy draft (proposal):
1) Maintain sprint buffer target: $250k (vote to carry into Q1 FY27).
2) Contingent hire pool: pre-authorize up to 12 contractor-months (aggregate) without exec sign-off for quick onboarding; finance to cap at $120k spend before review.
3) Triggers: automatic buffer payout if 7-day rolling token volume > +30% AND projected spend delta (on-demand routing) > $30k.
4) If buffer draw > $100k or multiple sequential draws inside 60d, escalate to Head of Finance and CTO for decision on hiring conversion.

Operational workbook snapshot (fields for automation):
- metric_token_7d_delta_pct: 0.0
- projected_infra_delta_usd: 0.0
- buffer_balance_usd: 250000
- contractors_onboarded: 0
- contingency_spend_30d: 0
(note: above are column headers in downstream automation; included here for product integration planning)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a differential buffer by region (NA/EU/APAC)? APAC burst cost is ~1.2x due to smaller inventory — proposal: keep 20% of buffer fungible but tag $50k for APAC.
- How fast can TalentOps onboard contractors (SLA)? Current anecdote: 10 business days; verify with Ops.
- Integrate with pricing engine: quick button to enable per-route throttling or price-tiering for specific customers — engineering estimate required.
- Formalize post-mortem metric set for each buffer draw (latency, revenue impacted, customer credits).

Appendix: sample contractor vs. perm math (12-week view):
- Perm cost (fully burdened): $220k/year -> 3 months cost = $55k (salary accural) + hiring overhead (estimate $25k) => $80k
- Contractor equivalent: 3 months = $30k
- Conversion cost if hire perm after contractor: recruiting + ramp = additional $20k - $40k depending on funnel; net often favors contracting for <12w events.

Notes to reviewers (Hannah):
- Please call out any objections to buffer sizing or the $120k pre-authorize contractor cap.
- Miguel: can you sanity-check marginal per-token figures vs. infra team numbers?
- Priya: talent ops SLA and typical contractor conversion time?
- Owen: flag any accounting implications for recognizing buffer as restricted vs. free cash (we prefer restricted cap to avoid creative reallocation).

Next steps:
- Sync with Infra on marginal cost inputs (due 2026-12-20).
- Build simple Google Sheet that wires real-time token metrics to the workbook fields above (owner: Finance Ops).
- Pilot approach in Jan sprint for 60d window; collect PM feedback and actual cost deltas.

End of sheet.
